basis.governing_question: How can Metalúrgica Norte cut conversion cost across its six plants in Portugal and Spain and put the improvements in place in every plant?

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Establish where conversion cost per part arises in each plant and size the improvements that would reduce it.

gate.label: Initiative go/no-go
gate.decision: Go or no-go on the sized improvements, and which plant pilots them first?

phases.name: Implementation
phases.objective_one_line: Carry out the approved improvements at a pilot plant, roll them out to the other plants, and track savings.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Approve the final results and the running improvements in all six plants?

workstreams.name: Baseline, first two plants
workstreams.answers: Where does conversion cost per part sit in the first two plants diagnosed, and what drives it?
activities: Build the cost per part baseline from operational data
Observe lines and interview the people who run them
Trace conversion cost losses to their causes by line

workstreams.name: Baseline, third plant
workstreams.answers: Where does conversion cost per part sit in the third plant diagnosed, and what drives it?
activities: Apply the first-round method to the third plant
Observe the lines and interview the people who run them
Compare its loss causes with those of the first two plants

workstreams.name: Baseline, other three plants
workstreams.answers: Where does conversion cost per part sit in the other three plants, estimated from their data?
activities: Collect cost and production data for these plants
Extend the loss patterns found on the floor to their data
Test the estimates with the people who run each plant

workstreams.name: Cost improvement sizing
workstreams.answers: Which improvements, sized per plant, cut conversion cost per part by a measurable amount in every plant?
activities: List improvement options from loss causes with plant teams
Size the cost per part saving of each option by plant
Set out the go/no-go case and the pilot plant options

workstreams.name: Pilot plant improvements
workstreams.answers: Do the approved improvements show savings in the cost data at the pilot plant?
activities: Prepare the changes for go-live at the pilot plant
Launch the changes after the readiness workshop
Show the savings in cost data against the baseline

workstreams.name: Improvement rollout, wave 1
workstreams.answers: How are the improvements put in place in the first wave of plants?
activities: Adapt the piloted changes to each plant in the wave
Put the changes in place and train each plant's own teams
Track cost per part in each plant against its baseline

workstreams.name: Improvement rollout, wave 2
workstreams.answers: How are the improvements put in place in the remaining plants, so all six run them?
activities: Apply wave 1 lessons to the changes for each plant
Put the changes in place and train each plant's own teams
Track cost per part in each plant against its baseline

workstreams.name: Cost per part results
workstreams.answers: What conversion cost per part does each plant show against its baseline once the improvements run?
activities: Measure cost per part from plant data after wave 2
Compare each of the six plants with its baseline
Prepare the final readout with the COO and Plant Directors

deliverables.name: Cost per part baseline and loss causes, first two plants
Cost per part baseline and loss causes, third plant
Estimated cost per part baseline, other three plants
Sized cost per part improvements by plant
Go/no-go case with baseline, sizing and pilot plant options
Pilot plant change plan for the approved improvements
Prepared pilot changes and readiness record
Pilot go-live record and savings in cost data
Wave 1 go-live and training record with cost per part
Wave 2 go-live and training record with cost per part
Cost per part by plant against its baseline
Final readout: results and running improvements, six plants

events.label: Kick-off
events.purpose: Start baseline work and secure plant access
attendees: Plant Directors of the six plants
events.decision: Confirm access to plant cost data and plant teams for the baseline work?
agenda: Present the engagement objective and the two phases
Discuss the cost data and plant contacts the baselines need
Confirm access to cost data and plant teams

events.label: Workshop 1: plant baselines
events.purpose: Review baselines and where cost arises
attendees: Plant Directors of the six plants
events.decision: Which loss causes should the improvement sizing detail first?
agenda: Present cost per part baselines for the six plants
Discuss loss causes and the estimated baselines
Decide which loss causes the sizing details first

events.label: Initiative go/no-go
attendees: Plant Directors of the six plants
events.decision: Go or no-go on the sized improvements, and which plant pilots them first?
agenda: Present the sized improvements by plant
Review the go/no-go case and the pilot plant options
Decide go or no-go and the pilot plant

events.label: Check-in: pilot change plan
attendees: Plant Directors of the six plants
events.decision: Confirm the pilot change plan as the basis for preparing the changes?
agenda: Present the pilot plant change plan
Discuss open points before preparation continues
Confirm the plan for preparing the pilot changes

events.label: Workshop 2: pilot and waves
events.purpose: Review pilot readiness and set rollout waves
attendees: Plant Directors of the six plants
events.decision: Which plants form wave 1 and wave 2 of the rollout after the pilot?
agenda: Review the pilot change plan and readiness record
Align on the cost per part measure for tracking savings
Decide wave 1 and wave 2 plants from sizing by plant

events.label: Check-in: wave 2 start
attendees: Plant Directors of the six plants
events.decision: Go or no-go on starting wave 2 at the planned plants, given the pilot savings?
agenda: Present the pilot go-live record and savings
Review how savings show in the cost data
Decide whether wave 2 starts as planned

events.label: Workshop 3: rollout results
events.purpose: Review results ahead of the final readout
attendees: Plant Directors of the six plants
events.decision: Which plant results and open points should the final readout detail?
agenda: Review pilot, wave 1 and wave 2 go-live records with cost per part
Align on how results are measured against each baseline
Decide which results and open points to detail

events.label: Final readout
attendees: Plant Directors of the six plants
events.decision: Approve the final results and the running improvements in all six plants?
agenda: Present cost per part by plant against its baseline
Review the final readout of results and running improvements
Decide on approval of the results and improvements

architect_notes: The brief gives no engagement length, so the 30 to 34 weeks are an estimate from the work sizing, not a stated length.
Implementation takes the middle of a 20 to 30 week estimate; 12-week pilot, 6-week waves and a 6-week window would push it to the top.
Diagnostic assumes three representative plants are diagnosed on the floor and the other three extended from data; which plants is open.
No Measurement phase: a savings window after the last wave runs inside Implementation, so tracking beyond it needs the partner's decision.

sub_questions.question: Where does conversion cost per part sit in each plant today, and what drives it?
Which improvements, sized per plant, cut conversion cost per part by a measurable amount in every plant?
Do the approved improvements show savings in the cost data at the pilot plant?
How are the improvements put in place in the other plants so they are running in all six plants?
What conversion cost per part does each plant show against its baseline once the improvements run?

drivers.evidence: six plants in Portugal and Spain

phases.name: Diagnostic

work.unit: Site diagnosed on the floor (cost baseline, line observation, loss analysis)

phases.why: Three plants diagnosed two at a time, the other three extended from data; above typical 3-6 weeks because three plants need two rounds.

phases.name: Implementation

work.unit: Pilot site: changes made and savings shown in the cost data
Rollout wave of up to 3 sites
Conversion cost per part measured after the last wave goes live

phases.why: Pilot, two waves in sequence, then a window after wave 2 (earlier windows overlap the next wave); above typical 8-16 weeks: work adds up.

sizing.levers: Running the two rollout waves side by side would cut the most; diagnosing two plants instead of three saves about two weeks.
